title: American Housing Survey distinguishes detached and multi-unit housing
content: The 2023 American Housing Survey defines and measures housing structure types including one-unit detached homes and multi-unit buildings. Security concepts should therefore avoid treating the United States as one uniform dwelling type.

title: Consumer IoT security applies to the whole product
content: NIST IR 8425 frames a consumer IoT product as the device plus supporting components and defines cybersecurity outcomes for consumer IoT products used at home or personally. A future security product must cover device, gateway, app and service boundaries.

title: Private indoor camera views create explicit privacy risk
content: The FTC advises consumers to consider security and privacy before installing connected cameras, especially when a camera shows private parts of a home such as a bedroom.

title: Home network security is part of connected-device safety
content: FTC consumer guidance highlights router configuration, encryption, unique credentials and software updates as important protections for internet-connected home devices.

title: Detached-home layouts create multiple security zones
content: For U.S. detached-home households, front doors, yards, garages and secondary entrances can create separate zones whose events must be combined to reconstruct an incident. This is a project hypothesis to validate by dwelling segment.

title: DIY installation can constrain setup complexity
content: A U.S. direct-to-consumer security concept may face adoption friction if calibration, wiring or professional installation is required. This channel assumption must be tested rather than treated as a market fact.

title: Package events are a distinct entry-area job
content: Doorstep delivery can create a security job spanning arrival detection, identity uncertainty, dwell time and removal. The incidence and willingness to pay must be validated for the chosen U.S. household segment.

title: Subscription value must remain legible between incidents
content: A recurring U.S. security service risks churn when benefits are visible only during rare emergencies. Continuous value and a hardware-only baseline should be compared in commercial validation.

title: Outdoor sensing must survive environmental variation
content: Security concepts intended for yards and exterior entries must treat weather, lighting, animals, wireless range and battery life as interacting causes of missed events and false alarms.

title: Security automation needs reversible defaults
content: Automations that unlock, sound alarms or contact others can create harm when context is wrong. High-impact actions should require explicit approval or a reversible, audited policy boundary.
